title: Documentation lanes: folder is lifecycle state, with a skill codifying the flow
head: mse_djvwtfx02kjr5j1n:d2
current_summary: Documentation folders are lifecycle lanes - intake, active planning, live spec, reference, and terminal outcomes. An active proposal carries a status block and completion criteria; a completed one moves lane with its supersession pointers intact. A seeded `proposal_lifecycle` skill codifies the flow and its gates.
current_why: The lanes had been reorganised ad hoc across several sessions, leaving stale cross-references and unclear boundaries. Making the folder the state, and enforcing it through a reusable skill, keeps the roadmap discoverable, prevents duplicate work, and makes proposal status readable without opening every document.

live_chain.title: D2 - Author the functionality audit with data-flow diagrams
live_chain.body: - D: Authored `docs/functionality-audit.md` — every current feature (CLI, agent-selective install, runtime, routing, skills, personas, hooks, MCP retrieval + ranking, session model, versioning, doctor, orphan sweep, release) plus 7 mermaid diagrams (system map, init/update, MCP pipeline, session lifecycle, agent wiring, multi-user layout, roadmap) and an upcoming-features section (2.8.0 ESR generalization; 3.0 multi-user memory + Memory Explorer). - R: User requested a full audit with data-flow diagrams covering current + upcoming features. title: DRAFT single-decision baseline; D/R mandatory; numbered decisions canonical
head: ms-db2d715c:d1
current_summary: The single-decision DRAFT record is the baseline session-entry shape. D/R (Decision/Rationale) are mandatory fields; A/F/T (Alternatives/Findings/Tests) are optional. Multi-decision entries use numbered #### Dn headings as the canonical form.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "Use `D`, `R`, `A`, `F`, and `T` labels for decision, rationale, alternatives, files/artifacts/behaviors, and tests/validation" (ms-db2d715c:d1). Institutes the DRAFT label vocabulary that makes D/R mandatory in all decision records.

live_chain.title: D1 - Use DRAFT for compact decision records
live_chain.body: - D: Use `D`, `R`, `A`, `F`, and `T` labels for decision, rationale, alternatives, files/artifacts/behaviors, and tests/validation. - R: The user wanted the same decision-history function with fewer tokens and less semantic-search noise from repeated long labels. - A: Rejected keeping verbose labels such as `Decision:` and `Alternatives considered:` because they add repeated non-domain terms before the content. - F: `.memory-seed/agent-rules.md`, `.memory-seed/project-bootstrap.md`, `.memory-seed/skills/memory_consolidation.md`, seed copies, and this session entry. - T: `python -m unittest tests.test_session_schema`; `python -m unittest discover -s tests`; `python -m memory_seed.cli doctor`; `python -m memory_seed.cli init --dry-run`.

title: edge_confidence on machine-suggested edges; consumers fade low tiers
head: mse_p4xd3wqf214nqtmv:d2
current_summary: Every machine-suggested lifecycle edge carries a structured `edge_confidence` entry of `{ref, confidence, tier}` keyed to the exact edge token, stored as YAML rather than prose. `links check` tolerates it as an unknown sibling key with no parser change. Consumers read it: the Trace graph and Trail fade low-confidence edges by opacity so an unverified suggestion never renders as settled fact, while authored edges carry no confidence attribute and render at full strength.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "Each campaign edge carries its model confidence in a new `edge_confidence:` list of `{ref, confidence, tier}` mappings" (mse_p4xd3wqf214nqtmv:d2). Created the structured edge_confidence field that the ADR governs.

live_chain.title: D2 - Store per-edge confidence as a structured edge_confidence field, consumption deferred
live_chain.body: - D: Each campaign edge carries its model confidence in a new `edge_confidence:` list of `{ref, confidence, tier}` mappings - structured YAML, not prose - keyed to the exact edge token. The `note:` keeps only provenance and the block's overall status. `links check` tolerates the field with no parser change; teaching the graph to read it is a deliberately deferred later stage. - R: Discarding low-confidence edges wastes paid-for work; writing them indistinguishably from human-authored edges would let a guess masquerade as fact. A structured field lets a later graph stage weight or filter them without re-parsing prose. A probe confirmed the parser scans only known ref-list keys, so the unknown sibling key is invisible to it (integrity OK with it present) - storing now costs nothing and needs no read-side change.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Client render for edge confidence (stage 2, completing "teach the graph and Trail to read the confidence"). GraphWorkspace fades machine-suggested edges by confidence via cytoscape data-driven styles - low (<0.7) -> opacity 0.28 + thin, mid (0.7-0.9) -> 0.5, high/authored -> full 0.85; TrailWorkspace folds a confidence factor into arc opacity (low x0.5, mid x0.75). Authored edges (no confidence) render full strength; a hovered/selected edge is never dimmed. Verified live against the restarted backend: of 60 visible graph edges, all 13 low-confidence edges sit at opacity <0.35, 10 mid at ~0.5, 28 authored/high at full - exactly the intended weighting. - R: The campaign's whole point was to keep weak edges but never let them read as settled fact; fading them by confidence delivers that in the view the user actually looks at. Handled the cytoscape null-coercion trap explicitly - a null `confidence` attribute coerces to 0 in a `[confidence < x]` selector, which would silently fade every authored edge, so the attribute is OMITTED (not null) when unscored. Rebuilt the committed static/react bundle so the packaged app serves it. - A: Considered a settings threshold/filter control; deferred per the design review (ship the default weighting first, add a filter only if asked). Considered line-style for confidence; rejected because line-style already encodes edge type (related/replaces/evolves). - F: memory-trace/client/src/{GraphWorkspace.tsx, TrailWorkspace.tsx}, memory-trace/memory_trace/static/react (rebuilt bundle) - T: client typecheck; live browser - no console errors, payload carries confidence (375 scored), cytoscape edge opacities match the tiers

title: Four never-merged edge kinds, forward-only and acyclic
head: mse_0qycwt519qdggrpe:d1
current_summary: Lifecycle edges comprise four never-merged kinds: `replaces`, `evolves`, `related_entries`, and `evolved_by` (inverse). Edges are forward-only and acyclic by contract.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "`DEFAULT_GRAPH_EDGE_TYPES` becomes `related, supersedes, evolves`" (mse_0qycwt519qdggrpe:d1). Institutes the three core edge kinds system by defining DEFAULT_GRAPH_EDGE_TYPES.

live_chain.title: D1 - Topic is not a relationship, so it is not a default edge
live_chain.body: - D: `DEFAULT_GRAPH_EDGE_TYPES` becomes `related, supersedes, evolves`. Topic remains offered. - R: The construction settles it. `chain()` in service.py groups entries by topic, sorts by time and joins CONSECUTIVE pairs, so a topic edge asserts "nothing else carrying this tag happened between these two" - a fact about sort order, not about the two entries. `related`/`supersedes`/`evolves` are authored claims about a specific pair. Topic membership is also already carried by node colour now that communities are named after topics, so drawing the chain renders the same fact twice and adds a pairwise link that does not exist. - R: The codebase had been compensating for this for a while. `topic` sits at priority 4 of 7 in `EDGE_PRIORITY`, below `branch`, and the pair-precedence rule exists because - in its own comment's words - a topic tag was painting over a supersession. Needing to suppress an edge type is evidence about the edge type. - A: The chain shape matters and my first instinct was wrong: I expected all-pairs and a combinatorial explosion. It is a chain, so 165 `memory-trace` entries make 164 edges, not 13,530. The problem is semantic, not quantitative.
